Output: New secondary school blocks constructed, and operated under EMO program Indicator: 100% of project secondary school blocks include gender-responsive features Progress/Status: This specific output of the project faced implementation delays mainly due to (i) COVID-19 pandemic outbreak shortly after the loan approval that disrupted the project activities due to restricted mobility; (ii) heavy monsoon rains in 2022 with combination of disastrous riverine flooding in Pakistan, particularly in the project area; and (iii) very frequent changes of project directors.
However, the procurement process of all 6 civil works contracts was completed in mid-2024 and civil works contracts were awarded of approximately $53 million, and the contractors were mobilized. During the last review mission in September 2024, the Mission observed slow progress on all 6 contracts, mainly due to late contractor mobilization, limited resource allocation by contractors, design changes, and unforeseen disruptions detailed below. However, during the recent mission in June 2025, the Mission noted improvement on three contracts, while significant improvement is still required on the remaining three contracts to achieve timely completion of the overall project. The Minister SELD, Chairman P&DD, and Secretary SELD recommended taking contractual action against underperforming contractors and consultants. The mission also noted some design issues along with the changes in the quantities of BOQ items. This is also observed that the supervision consultant did not discuss the increase in quantities of BOQ items and the associated costs with the PIU prior to execution. The construction supervision consultant and the PIU are currently collaborating to review, rationalize, and finalize these variations. The mission emphasized that, given the status of loan proceeds, there is minimal capacity to accommodate any contract variations or additional BOQ quantities using the loan funds. Any quantities exceeding the approved amount may require financing from the government's own resources.
During the Loan Review Mission in November 2025, it was observed that while progress on 3 contracts was satisfactory and that construction would likely be completed within the current loan closing date, progress for the remaining 3 contracts is insufficient and they are unlikely to be completed by the specified period, and the loan is to be extended by 18 to 24 months to allow for the completion of physical works. Data Source: Data from PIU Actual value:

Output: Secondary education examination system strengthened Indicator: At least 80% of BISE assessors, of which 40% are female, pass a competency test in item writing and examination development Progress/Status: Training of 427 examination assessors and paper setters from the Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISEs) has been completed, while training for 2,630 teachers in five key subjects is ongoing. The training covered procedures for setting and moderating questions, preparing question papers, developing answer keys and marking schemes, awarding partial marks, item-writing, critical thinking, and gender sensitivity. A pretest and posttest were conducted before and after the training. Data Source: Special pre- and post-training competency tests Actual value:

Output: New secondary school blocks constructed, and operated under EMO program Indicator: Proportion of secondary schools in Sindh with a (i) science laboratory increases to 30%, (ii) library increases to 20% Progress/Status: L3845: On track to be achieved, The 100 SEF Schools (Sindh Education Foundation) have received laboratory equipment from the supplier hired by the SSEIP (Sindh Secondary Education Improvement Project). Furthermore, the Sindh Education Literacy Department has successfully supplied laboratory equipment to the 400 existing government schools.
Furthermore, Science Laboratory is included in the building design, and Equipment shall be provided to SSEIP schools. ii-A Digital Library cum Computer laboratory is included in the design of the school block.
Percentage progress calculation will be done in 2025.
Data Source: Annual school census data (source: SELD) Actual value:

Output: New secondary school blocks constructed, and operated under EMO program Indicator: Updated education PPP framework, including revised PPP governance arrangements, strengthened PPP node, and streamlined EMO contracting process, approved by SELD Progress/Status: L3845: According to the Annual School Census (ASC) of 2016-17, there is a total of 1,706 secondary schools in Sindh. The SSEIP project aims to serve 630-660 schools, which includes 100 SEF schools supported by the project, 400 government schools funded by the government, and an estimated 130-160 SSEIP project schools. By adopting this approach, the SSEIP project strives to increase the availability of science laboratories from a baseline of 22% to an estimated 37-38% and library facilities from a baseline of 12% to an estimated 28-29% against the project's plan. Data Source: Government notification of updated education PPP framework Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Secondary education examination system strengthened Indicator: Newly developed uniform examination syllabus and specifications for grades 9-12 approved by Universities and Boards Department and BISE Progress/Status: The Uniform Examination Syllabus (UES) for grades 9 and 10 in the five key subjects was notified by the Curriculum Council, SE&LD, on 23 December 2025. The Minister for Education has also publicly announced the notification through the press.
The UES for grades 11 and 12 in the same subjects has been reviewed by DCAR, and all observations have been incorporated. The revised UES was submitted to the Sindh Curriculum Council on 27 January 2026 for notification. The notification is expected to be issued within the coming week, subject to the Council's endorsement. Data Source: Government notification of revised examination syllabus and specifications Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Secondary education examination system strengthened Indicator: Optical mark recognition systems for grades 9-12 examinations adopted by Sindh BISE Progress/Status: The Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISEs) have piloted the use of Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) and e marking systems for selected examination papers. BISE Shaheed Benazirabad and BISE Sukkur have implemented the systems across seven subjects, including science, for grades 9 and 11. Other BISEs have introduced OMR and e marking in at least one subject per designated grade as part of the phased rollout. While the pilot demonstrates progress toward modernizing assessment processes, examination reforms continue to face resistance and operational challenges, which may affect the pace of scale up across all BISEs.
Key Challenges include Insufficient scanning equipment, limiting timely processing of OMR sheets. Recurring costs associated with generating, storing, and managing digital copies. Shortage of trained e marking assessors, requiring large scale training and capacity development. Assessment gaps in compulsory subjects (e.g., Pakistan Studies, Islamic Studies, Urdu/Sindhi), including the need to update Uniform Examination Syllabi (UES) and Tables of Specifications (ToS). And, Limited readiness in commerce and computer subjects, particularly regarding UES alignment, ToS development, and adaptation to E marking protocols. Data Source: Data from BISE Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Teaching capacity in five key subjects improved Indicator: Teacher training and mentoring program in five key subjects (English, mathematics, biology, chemistry, and physics) developed, incorporating gender-sensitive strategies Progress/Status: Output 2 remains on track. Training for 2,445 secondary teachers across the five key subjects has been completed. Training was delivered in 11 of 12 cycles, and the twelfth cycle is currently underway. The target is expected to be achieved by 7 February 2026. Data Source: Data from PIU Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
